brief: Following WSJ reporting that NVIDIA's board is preparing to remove Jensen Huang as CEO after NYT reported an extramarital relationship with Kimberly Powell, VP of Healthcare, who reports to him, and Bloomberg reporting NVDA hired an outside firm to identify candidates and may name an interim CEO, Wells Fargo says a CEO change is increasingly likely, expecting CFO Colette Kress as the probable interim choice (with VP of Hyperscale & HPC Ian Buck gaining visibility) during an internal/external search. WF is reluctant to call the change a clearing event for shares but sees little/no demand-destruction risk and stays confident in out-year estimates, given NVIDIA's supply-chain scale and efficiency gains, which it argues can sustain growth and market share without Huang and justify a premium valuation versus SOX. It flags unresolved questions: whether NVIDIA's ~60-direct-report structure under Huang is repeatable under a new CEO (slower coordination), whether AI-investment pace changes since Huang drove many deals personally, and government scrutiny of sales to Megaspeed, calling that a likely drawn-out risk pending the 11/18 closed-door briefing. WF maintains Overweight and a $300 target (~15x 2028E P/E), but lists Huang key-person risk.
